answer: Each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, each result depending on the previous one; a Wesolowski proof lets others verify the delay efficiently. GPUs can run separate clones concurrently, but cannot shortcut a clone’s chain, so more identities require more total work. This is a haven against cheap Sybil floods, not the summit of security: parallel hardware boosts throughput, not per-identity speed, even if its advantage is more than a whisper.
